profiles: All nine MySQL releases and modes pinned by server-projection-v1.json.
requiredScope: All fixed syntax, version and role obligations remain in force.

From/Join.role: An ordered comma product of checked FROM items.
From/Join.structure: A left-associated CROSS tree with each already associated member retained as a subtree. Parenthesized product members keep their containment.
From/Join.conditions: Each ordinary source and nested supported join closes its own references. An explicit ON condition sees only its two operand subtrees. The complete statement checks occurrence and expression budgets.
From/Join.meaning: The list takes the row product in source-occurrence order for field layout. Explicit JOIN binds before comma. Each outer operand extends only its own side's results before the list product.
From/Join.sql: Emit explicit parenthesized CROSS and existing scoped JOIN syntax. Generate a distinct alias for each leaf.

ResultColumn.role: A named result slot over a comma product.
ResultColumn.structure: An ordered checked scalar with a fixed result heading.
ResultColumn.conditions: The chosen signed INT slot belongs to its resolved lexical table occurrence, including repeated declarations.
ResultColumn.meaning: The result preserves native names, positions, signed INT metadata, values, duplicates and NULL.
ResultColumn.sql: Reference the qualified physical field and preserve its declared label spelling.

externalInterpretation: The oracle and native queries use the same absolute table declarations, signed INT headings and fixture rows under the pinned session profile.
observations: Native result field names and indices, signed INT metadata and NULL
Rows with duplicate inputs, repeated aliases and empty operands
WHERE addresses full product scope while ON is local to its join's operands
Right and left unmatched rows expose physical fields in their declared order

finite.completeness: Require the full set of identities recovered from completed source trees, projection and filters on every release.

exploration.requiredForms: Vary operand layout, left or right extension, duplicate occurrence identity, slot positions, empty sources and nested member products.

analysis: A two-member list exposes both physical headings in order.
A qualified wildcard selects the third occurrence in a self product.
A WHERE comparison binds two aliases of the same declaration.
An empty member removes all combinations and preserves column metadata.
A lower-precedence comma preserves the RIGHT operand of a local LEFT join.
A lower-precedence comma preserves the local RIGHT join and post-product WHERE.
A parenthesized product is the left operand of an outer join.
A parenthesized product on the right of a comma preserves association and fields.
negative: A direct scoped result makes an out-of-range occurrence reference.
An ON condition attempts to use a preceding comma item.
An unqualified field is ambiguous across two list items.
A comma item resolves to no declared relation.
A comma list exceeds the checked input budget.
faults: Read a later occurrence from the first table
Lose a local LEFT join's unmatched rows
Omit WHERE after the complete product

evidence.P01: Compare exact occurrence-local field identities and local ON references.
evidence.P02: Check bounds and closed operand scopes before publication.
evidence.P03: Store the ordered checked operands without the parse tree.
evidence.P04: Calculate local matched and unmatched rows before the Cartesian product.
evidence.P05: Use the closed immutable join, field and result roles.
evidence.P06: Observe original and emitted SQL on the pinned releases.
evidence.Q01: Require typed rejection at the established owner for each negative.
evidence.Q02: Require the declared finite product, seeded cases and analyzed positives.
evidence.Q03: Check clause precedence, scoped input occurrences and observable NULL extension.
evidence.Q04: Replay field metadata and typed bags against the independently paired rows.
evidence.Q05: Record selected controller, distribution bytes and exact applied fault patches.

open: Lateral references, unsupported operands, additional key types and terms above the documented bound remain in scope and require evidence.
trust: Pinned MySQL grammar and database profile
Audited source closure and exact candidate controller linkage
